sections.title: Identification and habitat
sections.text: The catalogue entry Cichorium refers to Cichorium intybus, common chicory, rather than the whole genus. This perennial with a long taproot reaches about 1 m. Native to Europe, North Africa and western and central Asia, it is now widespread on roadsides and disturbed ground. Its blue flower heads consist entirely of strap-shaped florets.

sections.title: Edible leaves and roots
sections.text: Leaves and roots of some cultivated groups are eaten; chicory roots can be roasted and ground as a coffee substitute. The plate shows the flowering plant and dry fruits, but not the long root or vegetable cultivars. Do not confuse it with Cichorium endivia, a different species grown as salad greens.
